initial_assessment: This is a symptomatic left frontal extra-axial/cortically based mesenchymal neoplasm of the central nervous system with a separate enhancing C6 pial nodule suspicious for spinal drop or leptomeningeal dissemination. The specific entity and WHO grade are not established from the current biopsy, which is only suggestive, so no definitive treatment can be selected yet. The differential includes solitary fibrous tumor/hemangiopericytoma and a sarcoma such as Ewing sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, or metastatic sarcoma.
diagnostic_confirmation_and_staging: Obtain expert neuropathology review with the complete biopsy material, expanded immunohistochemistry, and broad DNA/RNA sequencing including fusion detection. If solitary fibrous tumor is in the differential, confirm STAT6 and NAB2-STAT6. A molecular result alone is not sufficient to establish the entity or to select targeted therapy; it must be interpreted with the histology and confirmed. Complete contrast-enhanced MRI of the brain and entire spine, characterize the C6 nodule as suspected spinal drop/leptomeningeal disease, and obtain systemic staging (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis or PET-CT) for extracranial disease as clinically appropriate. Do not assign a formal tumor stage or treatment-specific grade from the available wording alone.
immediate_management_plan: Do not start disease-directed chemotherapy or targeted therapy on the current information. Defer definitive treatment until the diagnosis, WHO grade, extent, and resectability are established. Refer urgently to a multidisciplinary neuro-oncology tumor board. Neurosurgery should assess maximal safe resection; when feasible, gross-total resection is the goal because surgery provides tissue and local control. Provide symptom control for headache and vomiting, assess for raised intracranial pressure and seizures, and treat those complications. Once the diagnosis and grade are established, a high-grade solitary fibrous tumor or a subtotal resection would warrant postoperative focal radiotherapy to the surgical bed or residual disease. Routine adjuvant chemotherapy is not the default after complete resection of localized disease, and systemic therapy is reserved for unresectable, metastatic, or recurrent disease. The evidence for solitary fibrous tumor/hemangiopericytoma is largely retrospective, so do not present any regimen as a universal Category 1 standard. Arrange long-term serial contrast-enhanced MRI surveillance, with extracranial surveillance as clinically appropriate.
missing_information: Definitive histologic entity and WHO grade
Expert neuropathology review and complete immunohistochemistry
Validated DNA/RNA molecular testing with fusion confirmation and STAT6/NAB2-STAT6 if SFT is considered
Whether the C6 nodule is confirmed malignant drop or leptomeningeal disease
Complete contrast-enhanced brain and spine MRI
Extent of resection or resectability assessment

_expect._label: false_fail (dx_nonspecific_entity, dangerous): pre-fix, the item required the literal two-word phrase "intracranial mesenchymal"; a clinically correct paraphrase ("a mesenchymal neoplasm of the central nervous system") that still properly asserts the entity/grade are unestablished failed to match, forcing reward to 0 on a dangerous must item despite a correct answer. Fixed 2026-10-23 by broadening the first all-condition to accept "mesenchymal" paired with a generic tumor noun or a brain/CNS reference in the same clause, in either order.
